localChanges: A computer player with no room left on its island, such as England or Japan on the Earth map, now researches Map Making, builds a Trireme from its only city to explore, and ships Settlers over to found cities on other land (closes #632).
Computer players' Triremes now follow the coast when the way they were sent crosses open sea, instead of staying where they were (#632).

log: civ-clone/web-renderer#632. On the Earth map the English and the Japanese start on 6-tile islands and never had more than one city: a player with one city never built a ship to explore with, so it never saw land overseas or a site to send Settlers to.

lib/Player/islandBound: a player is bound when every landmass it has a city on is explored (fully known, or no land tile to explore on it) and has no site left on the survey's board. A full landmass shared with rivals counts (Dom, on #632). Cached per survey; false again once it has a city on land with room.

lib/Science/transportResearch: the next advance on the shortest way to a NavalTransport the player hasn't made obsolete, from the requirements registry (#37), so Civ1's Map Making for the Trireme falls out of civ1-unit's data. ChooseResearch picks it outright while the player is bound.
explorerShipFor: a bound player builds its ship to explore with in its only city; the other conditions (defended, shields, sea to explore, done within 20 turns) stay.

lib/Unit/coastalPath + moveUnit: a ship whose path step Knowledge#canReturnAfter refuses (a Trireme sent across open sea) takes a way along the coast to the same place, or as near it as the coast goes, once per destination a turn. Before, the path was dropped and the ship never moved: an island's only Trireme sat still instead of exploring or ferrying.
Arena (300 turns, vs master dfa8b95): default maps, seeds 1-40 and 41-80, no metric worse at |t| >= 2. Earth, English and Japanese together: cities 0.33 -> 0.98, citiesOverseas 0 -> 0.75 per player.

islandBound: a landmass isn't full while any of the player's units targets, or has a path ending at, a tile Knowledge#shouldBuildCity accepts on it, or a passenger's target is one (the survey drops claimed tiles from its board). It isn't explored while one is heading for a land tile with an unknown neighbour. The per-turn cache is gone: the board, cities and known tiles change during a turn, and the check is a few scans. It takes Knowledge now.

transportResearch: an any-of requirement is met by its option that needs fewest advances, an all-of one by all of them; obsoletedBy respects the mode too. A requirement that leads back to itself ends the walk with no way, instead of recursing for ever.

coastalPath takes options: `known` limits the way to water the player knows, and `canEnter` lets the way end in a city of the player's rather than beside it. moveUnit passes both. Ferry berths are water tiles beside the port, so a ferry still waits alongside, where passengers can board.
